subject: Mapping models, latency budget, and token runway for onboarding
messages:
From: Alex Ramos <alex@lumenlytics.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-16T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Mapping models and latency budget for onboarding

Hi Irene / Monica,

Thanks for the onboarding kickoff yesterday — excited to get LumenLytics onto Redwood. To help our engineering team plan capacity on our side, can you confirm the model candidates you're planning to include in the initial shortlist, and the recommended context-length profile? A few specifics the team is asking for: 

- Typical prompt+response token mix per API call (ballpark)
- Expected concurrent users / RPS at launch (we have an internal estimate but want to align)
- Any latency tiers you expect to offer (p95 targets) and whether the higher-quality models will be behind a different route

I've attached the customer product brief and a CSV of sample prompts (lumen_sample_prompts.csv). Also attaching our procurement contact in case we need to align on contractual SLAs.

Can you send a recommended shortlist + a token runway estimate (30 / 90 / 180 day)? Goal: decide whether to start on Hosted with autoscale or reserve Dedicated capacity.

Best,
Alex
Product Lead — LumenLytics
attachments: lumen_sample_prompts.csv (csv, 42 KB)
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-16T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mapping models and latency budget for onboarding

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear ask. Quick reply with a proposed starter plan and then a short checklist of what's needed from LumenLytics to finalize sizing.

Proposed model shortlist (initial alpha):
- rwd-small-7b-quant (fast) — good for short Q&A, p95 ~ 120–180ms token processing on T4-like hardware; recommended default for low-cost endpoints
- rwd-std-13b (balanced) — better coherence for longer instructions, p95 ~ 220–350ms per chunk on the same infra
- rwd-hq-70b (high-quality) — for long-form summarization and extraction (we'll route to this only for routed calls)

Context-length profile (we recommend supporting both):
- Short interactions (default): 2k tokens context (prompt ~200 tokens, response ~150 tokens typical)
- Deep context (for docs/search+summarize): 8k tokens context (prompt often 1–2k, response 500–2k)

Ballpark token mixes per call (examples):
- Short: prompt 200 / response 150 => ~350 tokens/call
- Deep: prompt 1800 / response 800 => ~2600 tokens/call

Traffic assumptions for sizing (please confirm):
- We used Lumen's pre-kickoff estimate of 12k MAUs converting to ~6k daily active users and 1.5k peak-concurrent web sessions. If peak concurrency is ~200 active request slots, we'd size conservatively for 250 concurrent requests.

30/90/180 token runway (conservative):
- 30d: 250k — assumes soft launch to pilot groups (avg mix short:deep = 80:20)
- 90d: 1.1M — expected ramp with feature beta and integrations
- 180d: 3.2M — broader rollout, higher deep-context usage increasing token average

Latency tiers and routing suggestion:
- Default route: rwd-small-7b-quant (cost-optimized) with p95 SLO 350ms for token throughput (depends on parallelism)
- Fallback / quality route: rwd-std-13b or rwd-hq-70b for heavy jobs; recommend async/long-poll or streaming for >2k responses

Next steps checklist for LumenLytics:
- Confirm peak concurrency (250 is our current working assumption)
- Confirm % of calls expected to be deep-context vs short (80:20 used above)
- Share 24-hour token CSV sample (anonymized) or metrics export if you have one

I'll loop Ben (infra) for concrete throughput sizing and a recommendation on Hosted vs Dedicated based on your confirmed concurrency.

Best,
Irene Choi
Customer Success Manager — Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Mapping models and latency budget for onboarding — throughput/ops recs

Alex / team — Ben here (in infra/serving). Picking up from Irene's estimates and adding the concrete ops numbers you'd need to decide Dedicated vs Hosted.

Assumptions used for below: 80% short calls (~350 tokens), 20% deep (~2.6k tokens), peak concurrency 250 requests (as proposed). We also assume average tokens per second processing of ~400 tokens/sec per GPU session for rwd-small and ~200 tokens/sec for rwd-std-13b.

Sizing (conservative):
- If starting on Hosted with autoscale: expect cost-effective run at pilot scale — provision 8 concurrent rwd-small instances to handle p95 load, burst to rwd-std for ~15% of requests. This supports ~250 concurrent requests for short calls with headroom.
- If opting for Dedicated (recommended before GA at >5k DAU): recommend 2x A10-equivalent nodes with continuous pool sizing that maps to ~24 GPU sessions for rwd-small and 12 sessions for rwd-std. This gives predictable tail latency and easier policy routing.

Token runway (validated):
- 30d: ~300k tokens (matches Irene's conservative)
- 90d: ~1.2M tokens
- 180d: ~3.5M tokens

Operational notes / asks for LumenLytics:
- Share anonymized 24-hour call logs (timestamps + token counts) — we can run a quick histogram to validate batching and KV cache effectiveness.
- If docs upload flow exists, recommend a preprocessor that chunks at 1k tokens with overlap 128 tokens; that will shift average deep call from 2.6k -> ~1.4k per user interaction (better for cost).
- Recommend enabling prefix caching for frequently referenced docs to cut token egress by ~15–30%.

Attachments: latency-bench-0806.pdf (short bench across our flavors) — includes per-model throughput on A10/T4 equivalencies.

If you confirm concurrency and the docs-upload behavior, we can produce a short cost comparison matrix (Hosted vs Dedicated) and a recommended rollout plan (pilot -> staged GA). Happy to hop on a 30-min call tomorrow to finalize.

- Ben
Principal Infra Engineer — Redwood Inference
